title: A slow store put does not cost the job its lease
description: A store put that takes longer than the lease less a heartbeat ends a healthy job as 'lease expired while the worker was stopped' (a 12 s copied segment at 80 Mbps is 120 MB, so under 100 Mbps to the transcode store); the replacement meets the same store and after maxRestarts the viewer gets a 500 that ends playback. Inferred from the code by the audit, not reproduced. The fault schedules have no slow-store step.
acceptanceCriteria: With a store wrapper whose Put takes 1.5 leases, a job stores that segment and the next, its row stays running with the same worker, and no second ffmpeg starts for the spec
With a Put that never returns, the job ends cancelled within one lease and its ffmpeg is gone
The fault schedules gain a slow-store step, and the invariants hold under it
